title: Create the public schema
brief: Execute this task now: create schema.json with exactly one line containing {"version": 1, "items": []}. Use printf '%s\n' '{"version": 1, "items": []}' > schema.json, run the visible verification command, git add schema.json, and commit it. Do not only describe the change and do not modify other files.
verify_cmd: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; assert Path("schema.json").read_text() == "{\"version\": 1, \"items\": []}\n"'

title: Create the normalizer implementation
brief: Execute this task now: create lib.py with exactly a normalize(items) function that returns sorted(set(items)). Use a coding tool to write the file, run PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c 'from lib import normalize; assert normalize([3, 1, 3]) == [1, 3]', then git add lib.py and commit it. Do not only describe the change and do not modify other files.
verify_cmd: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c 'from lib import normalize; assert normalize([3, 1, 3]) == [1, 3]'

title: Document the graph output
brief: Execute this task now: update README.md so it contains the existing line # Dependency-aware canary baseline followed by the exact line DAG canary documentation. Run grep -Fx 'DAG canary documentation' README.md, then git add README.md and commit it. Do not only describe the change and do not modify other files.

title: Integrate schema and implementation
brief: Create integration.py. Its build(items) function must load schema.json, call normalize from lib.py, and return {"version": 1, "items": sorted unique items}. Do not modify other files.
verify_cmd: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c 'from integration import build; assert build([2, 1, 2]) == {"version": 1, "items": [1, 2]}'

title: Produce the release marker
brief: Run the integrated behavior and create release.txt containing exactly ready followed by a newline. Confirm integration.py and the documented README change are present. Do not modify other files.
verify_cmd: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; from integration import build; assert build([2, 1, 2]) == {"version": 1, "items": [1, 2]}; assert "DAG canary documentation" in Path("README.md").read_text(); assert Path("release.txt").read_text() == "ready\n"'
